summary: Implementation plan for the cross-session `lumen trends` CLI subcommand: a new CompactionEvent domain type and Cost::Serialize on lumen-model, ClaudeCodeAdapter compact_boundary parsing (including CRIT-LUMEN-192's malformed-event skip/record path), a new compaction_events table plus CompactionRepository wired into upsert_session's existing atomic transaction, a new TrendRepository (list_session_trend + count_sessions), and a Commands::Trends CLI handler covering the CRIT-LUMEN-187/188/189 error-precedence rules and CRIT-LUMEN-183/184/186/191 table+JSON rendering rules.

tasks.title: Cost Serialize Impl Producing {usd, priced} Shape
tasks.reasoning: CRIT-LUMEN-186 requires cost to serialize as `{"usd": <f64>, "priced": true}` or `{"usd": null, "priced": false}`. Cost currently has no Serialize impl (confirmed by reading economics.rs), and a `#[derive(Serialize)]` on the enum would produce `{"Priced": 1.5}` / `"Unpriced"` instead -- the wrong shape -- so a manual impl is required. Done standalone, ahead of TrendRepository/cmd_trends, so SessionTrendPoint can simply derive Serialize and embed a `Cost` field later without any extra glue.

Add, after the `impl Cost { ... }` block: `impl Serialize for Cost { fn serialize<S>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> where S: Serializer { let mut state = serializer.serialize_struct("Cost", 2)?; match self { Cost::Priced(v) => { state.serialize_field("usd", v)?; state.serialize_field("priced", &true)?; } Cost::Unpriced => { state.serialize_field("usd", &Option::<f64>::None)?; state.serialize_field("priced", &false)?; } } state.end() } }`.

tasks.title: ClaudeCodeAdapter: Parse Well-Formed compact_boundary Events With Transcript-Encounter Sequence
tasks.reasoning: Adds the happy-path parsing branch only, proving sequence is 0-based transcript-encounter order (not persisted-only order) by interleaving a non-compact_boundary system line that must NOT increment the counter. CRIT-LUMEN-192's skip/gap behavior for malformed events is deliberately deferred to TASK-TRENDS-004 so this task stays under 15 minutes and each test asserts one coherent behavior. Concrete field-shape decision (spec leaves the top-level envelope unstated beyond 'the compact_boundary system event'): the line has `"type":"system"` and `"subtype":"compact_boundary"`, with a nested `compactMetadata` object carrying camelCase `trigger`/`preTokens`/`postTokens`/`cumulativeDroppedTokens`/`durationMs` -- exactly the field names given in the spec's api_surface, following Claude Code's established camelCase system-event convention already used elsewhere in this adapter (`isSidechain`, `costUSD`).

tdd_steps.expected_failure: cargo test -p lumen-session --test test_claude fails: `assertion 'left == right' failed: left: 0, right: 2` (transcript.compaction_events is always empty -- no 'system' line_type branch exists yet).
tdd_steps.implementation: In crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/claude.rs: declare `let mut compaction_events: SmallVec<[CompactionEvent; 4]> = SmallVec::new(); let mut compaction_sequence: u32 = 0;` alongside the other accumulator locals near the top of parse_stream. Add a new branch after the existing `} else if line_type == "user" { ... }` block: `} else if line_type == "system" { let subtype = val.get("subtype").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or(""); if subtype == "compact_boundary" { let seq = compaction_sequence; compaction_sequence += 1; if let Some(meta) = val.get("compactMetadata").and_then(|m| m.as_object()) { if let (Some(trigger_str), Some(pre), Some(post), Some(dropped), Some(dur)) = (meta.get("trigger").and_then(|v| v.as_str()), meta.get("preTokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()), meta.get("postTokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()), meta.get("cumulativeDroppedTokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()), meta.get("durationMs").and_then(|v| v.as_u64())) { let trigger = if trigger_str == "auto" { Some(CompactionTrigger::Auto) } else if trigger_str == "manual" { Some(CompactionTrigger::Manual) } else { None }; if let Some(trigger) = trigger { compaction_events.push(CompactionEvent { sequence: seq, trigger, pre_tokens: pre, post_tokens: post, cumulative_dropped_tokens: dropped, duration_ms: dur }); } } } } }`. In the final `Ok(CanonicalTranscript { ... })` literal, replace `compaction_events: SmallVec::new(),` (added in TASK-TRENDS-001) with `compaction_events,`.

tasks.title: ClaudeCodeAdapter: Skip and Record Parse Failures for Malformed compact_boundary Events
tasks.reasoning: Proves the malformed branch left as a silent no-op by TASK-TRENDS-003 (the `if let Some(trigger) = trigger { ... }` with no else) now records a ParseFailureRecord instead of silently dropping the event, and that `compaction_sequence` still increments for the skipped event so persisted sequence has a visible gap (0, 2 -- not 0, 1) -- proving CRIT-LUMEN-185's 'gaps from skipped events' clause together with CRIT-LUMEN-192's own skip requirement. Covers all four malformed sub-cases textually (missing compactMetadata, missing/unparseable numeric field, bad trigger) via one representative test per the spec's own phrasing (each is 'OR'-joined into the same skip rule), keeping this task under 15 minutes; the missing-cumulativeDroppedTokens case is chosen as the concrete fixture since the spec's own reasoning cites it as the empirically-observed real-world case (17/112 real events).

tdd_steps.expected_failure: cargo test -p lumen-session --test test_claude fails: `assertion 'left == right' failed: left: 1, right: 2` (compaction_events.len() is 1, not 2 -- current code silently drops both the malformed line's event AND its parse-failure record, and TASK-TRENDS-003's raw sequence counter still incremented correctly but nothing surfaces the failure).
tdd_steps.implementation: In crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/claude.rs, replace the `if let (Some(trigger_str), ...) = (...) { ... } else { }`-shaped block from TASK-TRENDS-003 with explicit per-field error reporting. Concretely, restructure the compact_boundary branch body to: `match val.get("compactMetadata").and_then(|m| m.as_object()) { None => parse_failures.push(ParseFailureRecord { session_id: session_id.clone(), line_number, byte_offset: line_start_offset, error: CompactString::new(format!("compact_boundary event (sequence {seq}): missing compactMetadata")) }), Some(meta) => { let trigger_str = meta.get("trigger").and_then(|v| v.as_str()); let pre = meta.get("preTokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()); let post = meta.get("postTokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()); let dropped = meta.get("cumulativeDroppedTokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()); let dur = meta.get("durationMs").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()); let trigger = match trigger_str { Some("auto") => Some(CompactionTrigger::Auto), Some("manual") => Some(CompactionTrigger::Manual), _ => None }; let missing: Vec<&str> = [("trigger", trigger.is_some()), ("preTokens", pre.is_some()), ("postTokens", post.is_some()), ("cumulativeDroppedTokens", dropped.is_some()), ("durationMs", dur.is_some())].into_iter().filter(|(_, ok)| !ok).map(|(name, _)| name).collect(); if let (Some(trigger), Some(pre), Some(post), Some(dropped), Some(dur)) = (trigger, pre, post, dropped, dur) { compaction_events.push(CompactionEvent { sequence: seq, trigger, pre_tokens: pre, post_tokens: post, cumulative_dropped_tokens: dropped, duration_ms: dur }); } else { parse_failures.push(ParseFailureRecord { session_id: session_id.clone(), line_number, byte_offset: line_start_offset, error: CompactString::new(format!("compact_boundary event (sequence {seq}): invalid or missing field(s): {}", missing.join(", "))) }); } } }`.

tasks.reasoning: Base query without compaction support -- proves CRIT-LUMEN-190's ordering ('at most n most recent by started_at DESC, ties by provider_session_id ASC', 0-limit coerced to 50, matching list_recent) and CRIT-LUMEN-183's data-shape (cost/cache_hit_ratio/turn_count/has_anomalies per session, oldest-to-newest). cache_hit_ratio is rounded half-to-even to 1 decimal HERE, at the repository layer, via the `format!("{:.1}", v).parse()` trick (Rust's float formatting is a correctly-rounded, ties-to-even decimal conversion of the exact binary value -- the same guarantee this codebase's existing `format!("{:.1}%", ...)` renderer already relies on) -- so both the table and JSON renderers in TASK-TRENDS-013/014 consume an already-rounded value and cannot disagree or double-round. tasks.title: TrendRepository::list_session_trend -- CompactionSummary Population (Last-by-Sequence, Zero vs n/a)
tasks.reasoning: Replaces TASK-TRENDS-009's inert require_compaction branch with real per-session compaction aggregation. tokens_dropped_total is deliberately computed by iterating rows ordered by `sequence ASC` and keeping the last one seen -- not a SQL MAX() aggregate over cumulative_dropped_tokens -- because CRIT-LUMEN-184 requires 'the highest-sequence event that WAS persisted', and sequence (not the token value) is the ordering key; a value-based MAX would silently give the wrong answer whenever an earlier event happens to report a larger number than a later one. Non-Claude-Code sessions keep `.compaction = None` (n/a) even when require_compaction is true; Claude Code sessions with zero persisted events get `Some(CompactionSummary::zeros())`, never None -- the two 'nothing to report' cases stay distinguishable per the criterion's explicit requirement.
